results.rationale: Kennett 2009 documents shock-formed nanodiamonds/lonsdaleite at Younger Dryas boundary sediments including North American sites, directly supporting a corroborated cosmic-impact origin for the nanodiamond-concentration via impact-ejecta-fallout in North America. No contradiction present.

No supporting or refuting evidence is attached to this hypothesis. An empty evidence set is not itself a contradiction, and nothing in the broader evidence pool explicitly places platinum-anomaly/cosmic-airburst claims outside a Middle East locale or outside the -10850 bin.

Haile et al. 2009 shows mammoth and horse persisted in interior Alaska (North America) well past 12.9 ka, undermining a synchronous impact-triggered extinction pulse -- this is consistent with, not contradictory to, the hypothesis's claim that the cosmic-impact-driven megafaunal-extinction link is refuted. Alaska falls within the stated North America placement, so no geographic contradiction exists.

Pigati 2012 and Surovell 2009 both report failure to find a discrete, boundary-confined microspherule peak (continuous background accumulation, failed replication across sites), which is consistent with -- rather than contradictory to -- the hypothesis's claim that the cosmic-airburst/microspherule-concentration link is refuted. No actor/place/time contradiction is evident.

No evidence is attached to test the supernova-event actor, gamma-ray-ionization mechanism, Greenland placement, or the -13000/-12001 interval. No contradiction is present; the 'inconclusive' status is not undermined by any cited source.
